process_flow.agency_action: Conduct the assessment activities
Consolidate the results of the assessment activities and transmit the results and the appropriate rating sheets to the HRMPSB for rating
Rate all applicants individually based on their assessment results
Consolidate the ratings and prepare comparative assessment results matrix and Selection Line-up
Deliberate on the results of the comparative assessment and finalize the selection line-up for the appropriate action of the appointing authority
Prepare and sign the HRMPSB Resolution and Minutes
Transmit the selection line-up and the signed resolution and minutes to the appointing authority for formal selection.
Select the applicant to be appointed to the vacant position
Notify the applicants of the selection results
process_flow.processing_time: 3 working days upon receipt of selection results

notes: The applicant may be required to attend more than one assessment activity depending on the level of position.

title: City Profile: Overview, Contact Information, and Geography
text: Calamba, officially the City of Calamba, is a 1st class component city in the province of Laguna, Philippines, and serves as the regional center of the CALABARZON region. According to the 2020 census, it has a population of 539,671. Contact: New City Hall Complex, Bacnotan Road, Brgy. Real, City of Calamba, Laguna, 4027; (049) 545-6789; info@calambacity.gov.ph. Geographically, Calamba is bounded by Laguna de Bay to the east, Cabuyao to the north, Los Baños to the south, and Sto. Tomas and Tanauan (Batangas) to the west. It is only 54 kilometers from Metro Manila and is considered the premier industrial hub outside Metro Manila due to the large number of companies based there. Total land area is 14,480 hectares, with an urban expansion area of 8,526.7 hectares, covering 54 barangays (37 urban, 17 rural). As of the 2010 NSO count, total population was 389,377 with 223,241 registered voters. Major religious denominations: Roman Catholic (89.72%), Protestant (3.43%), Iglesia Ni Cristo (3.14%), Islam (0.26%), Others (3.45%). Land use breakdown (in hectares): Urban Redevelopment Area 2,080; Growth Management Area 1: 4,199; Growth Management Area 2: 2,460; Upland Conservation Area: 3,401.22; Forest Buffer Zone: 333; Forest Reservation Area: 579.78; Agricultural Development Area: 1,427; total 14,480 has. Basic facilities include 6 hospitals, 111 clinics, 9 diagnostic centers, 2 public markets, 3 recreational facilities, and 23 transportation facilities. Power supply is provided by Meralco and Napocor; water by Calamba Water District. Telecom providers include Globe, Smart, and SunCellular (cellular) and PLDT, Digitel, SunCellular (landline), with postal service via the Philippine Postal Corporation. Educational institutions include 16 technical/vocational schools, 17 universities and colleges, 21 public and 39 private high schools, and 51 public and 69 private elementary schools.

title: Historical Background and Legal Basis of Creation
text: Calamba was originally part of Tabuco (now Cabuyao) and became a separate pueblo on August 28, 1742 by Governatorial Decree. According to legend, the name 'Calamba' derives from 'kalan-banga,' referring to an earthen jar (banga) a young woman was carrying when a Guardia Civil asked for the name of the place; her answer about what she carried was mistaken for the place name, and 'Kalambanga' was later shortened to 'Calamba.' Calamba became a component city on April 21, 2001 by virtue of Republic Act No. 9024, signed into law by President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo on March 5, 2001 and ratified by plebiscite on April 21, 2001.

title: Economic Data
text: Calamba is classified as a First Class Component City. Annual income by year: 2015 – Php 2.59 Billion; 2014 – Php 2.2 Billion; 2013 – Php 1.95 Billion; 2012 – Php 1.7 Billion. Major income sources include manufacturing (industrial companies), agriculture (rice, corn, vegetables, root crops), services (manpower, metal craft), and tourism (hot spring resorts, Wonder Island, Rizal Shrine).

title: Tourist Destinations, Special Events, and Sister Cities
text: Notable tourist destinations include the Tallest Rizal Monument, hot springs, Wonder Island, Rizal Shrine, industrial parks, and clay pot (Banga) craftmaking. Special events and festivals include: April 21 – City Hood Anniversary/Banga Festival; June 12–19 – Buhayani Festival; June 12 – Independence Day; June 19 – Rizal Day/Rizal's Birth Anniversary; June 24 – Feast of St. John the Baptist/Basaan Festival; August 28 – Town Foundation of Calamba; December (month-long) – Paskuhan sa Calamba; December 30 – Rizal's Death Anniversary. Calamba's sister cities are Walnut City, California, USA; Wilhelmsfeld, Germany; Guri, South Korea; Geumcheon-gu, South Korea; and Litomerice, Czech Republic.

title: Political Data
text: The seat of government is the New City Hall Building, Brgy. Real, City of Calamba. Calamba is the lone congressional district of Laguna. As of August 2013, there were 723 clustered voting precincts.

title: History of Calamba's Cityhood (Republic Act No. 9024)
text: April 21, 2001 marked Calamba's conversion into the second component city of Laguna under Republic Act No. 9024, 'An Act Converting the Municipality of Calamba, Province of Laguna into a Component City to be known as the City of Calamba,' signed by President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo on March 5, 2001 at Malacañang Palace. COMELEC set the ratifying plebiscite for April 21, 2001, three weeks ahead of local elections. The push for cityhood began as early as 1994 when the Sangguniang Bayan passed Resolution No. 60 requesting Congress to co-sponsor a cityhood bill; Resolution No. 115 followed two years later. House Bill No. 986 and Senate Bill Nos. 1630 and 1791 were later filed by Congressman Joaquin M. Chipeco Jr. and Senators Franklin M. Drilon and Sergio Osmeña III respectively. The effort was fast-tracked in 2000 under then-Mayor Severino J. Lajara, with committee approval, public hearings (including one at Calamba Elementary School Central II), and eventual passage as House Bill No. 10661 and, in February 2001, as Republic Act No. 9024. The cityhood campaign involved posters, streamers, barangay patrol announcements, SPES student volunteers distributing flyers, bilingual brochures and comic strips from the City/Municipal Planning and Development Office, and information campaigns conducted across all 54 barangays from March 30 to April 19, 2001, addressing resident questions mainly about taxation and basic services. In the plebiscite, 15,056 Calambeños voted, with 3,413 (22.67%) voting 'No' and the remaining 77.33% voting 'Yes' to cityhood.

title: City Government Department List and Functions
text: The City Government of Calamba is organized into the following departments/offices: (1) City Administration Office – supervises city programs and provides administrative support to the Mayor; (2) Business Permits and Tricycle Franchising Office – processes business permits, working permits, and tricycle franchises; (3) City Accounting and Internal Control Office – handles accounting and internal audit; (4) Buildings Regulatory Services Department – enforces the National Building Code (P.D. 1096); (5) City Agricultural Services Department – implements agriculture/aquaculture programs and farmer assistance; (6) City Assessment Office – handles property assessment for local revenue; (7) City Budget Management Office – provides budgetary services; (8) City Civil Registry Office – manages civil registration; (9) City Engineering and Infrastructure Development Department – implements infrastructure projects; (10) City Environment and Natural Resources Office – manages natural resource conservation programs; title: Mission and Vision
text: Commitment and Direction: Shaping a smart, green, and inclusive future for every Calambeño. Mission: Work in partnership with its citizenry to deliver exceptional, effective, fiscally responsible, and gender-responsive services while preserving and protecting the environment and enhancing a high standard of community living. Vision: Calamba is a smart and green city with a progressive and inclusive economy where healthy, empowered, and God-centered people live in a secure, built, and natural environment under good governance.
